datasets.precomputed_features_note: The volume also holds features/phoenix14t.pami0.{train,dev,test}, which are the Camgoz et al. (2020b) sign embeddings. These are NOT the embeddings behind the target numbers: Table 2 row 1.1 shows that using Camgoz et al. (2020b) embeddings scores 21.21 B@4 on dev, whereas the SLTUNET result requires the authors' retrained SMKD embeddings with a 2D ResNet34 backbone (18.90 WER, row 15, 27.87 B@4). Reproducing the targets therefore requires SMKD pretraining from the videos in videos/, not reuse of these features. Using them instead would be a behaviour-changing protocol deviation and would reproduce a different table row.
datasets.frame_source_note: Important fidelity caveat found 2026-09-13. The shared Volume does not hold the original PHOENIX-2014T frame distribution. The authors' released test list points at PHOENIX-2014-T-release-v3/PHOENIX-2014-T/features/fullFrame-210x260px/test/<seq>/*.png, i.e. lossless PNG frames, and their published numbers were produced from those. The Volume instead holds videos/{train,dev,test}/<seq>.mp4: HEVC-encoded files muxed with Lavf 61.7.100, so they are a recent lossy re-encoding made by the study rather than the original pixels. One test sequence is 34 KB, indicating substantial compression. SMKD reads pixels directly, so compression artifacts can shift the extracted sign features and therefore the scores, by an amount that has not been measured. The original distribution remains available: https://www-i6.informatik.rwth-aachen.de/ftp/pub/rwth-phoenix/2016/phoenix-2014-T.v3.tar.gz returned HTTP 200 with Content-Length 41,699,758,035 and Last-Modified 2018-03-29 on 2026-09-13. No code change is needed to consume either form: the authors' own loader (smkd/dataset/dataloader_video.py BaseFeeder) branches on the path suffix and decodes MP4 through cv2.VideoCapture when the suffix is not jpg/png, so this is a path substitution rather than a patch.

datasets.storage_shape_finding: Worth knowing before any other paper stores frame-level data this way. The original distribution is roughly 1.2 million small PNG files, and the shared Modal Volume serves them at a measured 186 ms per cold file read (metadata is fast: 642 directory entries listed in 0.65 s and a 28-file glob in 0.05 s, so the cost is per-file reads, not lookups). Reading the 642-sequence test split directly through the data loader is therefore hours of latency rather than the 249 seconds the MP4 path took. The workaround used here is to bulk-copy the needed sequences to container-local disk once with 32-way parallelism and point the authors path list at the copies, which changes where bytes are read from and not what they contain. Even that staging is slower than a naive latency model predicts, which suggests the Volume throttles concurrent small reads. A better long-term shape for frame corpora on these Volumes is a small number of large archives per split, extracted locally at run time.

SMKD WER evaluation goes through smkd/evaluation/slr_eval/wer_calculation.evaluate, which requires the official PHOENIX ground-truth file {evaluation_prefix}-{mode}.stm even on its python path. No .stm ships in the sltunet repository, none exists in the shared Volume (the rwth-phoenix-2014 entry holds only raw/phoenix2014-release with annotations and features, no evaluation directory), and RWTH publishes no features-free archive for PHOENIX-2014T, only the full 41.7 GB phoenix-2014-T.v3.tar.gz. Building a substitute stm from the annotation CSV orth column was rejected: evaluation/slr_eval/preprocess.sh applies heavy PHOENIX-specific gloss normalisation to hypotheses, and whether the official reference carries the same normalisation is unknown, so a self-built reference would shift WER by an unquantified amount and the comparison against 18.90 would be uninterpretable. Consequence: the cheap diagnostic and the actual fix require the same download, so this gate and the WER check collapse into one decision.
gates.resolution: Reported resolved by the user on 2026-09-15: approval to add the uncompressed PHOENIX distribution. Acting on it by ADDING the original RWTH tree under rwth-phoenix-2014-t/raw/ rather than replacing the existing lossy videos, because other papers in this repository may depend on the current entries. The original also supplies PHOENIX-2014-T-groundtruth-{dev,test}.stm, which unblocks the SMKD WER diagnostic that was previously impossible.

environment_plan.published_requirements: python==3.8, tensorflow==1.15 (repository README 'Requirement'); no requirements.txt or lockfile is published.
environment_plan.base_image_conflict: The repository's standard GPU base image ghcr.io/sign-language-processing/reproduction:latest supplies NVIDIA NGC PyTorch. SLTUNET is TensorFlow 1.15, which needs CUDA 10.0 / cuDNN 7.x and will not run on that image, so a paper-specific Dockerfile is expected. This is an environment adaptation, not a change to the published code, and the exact image has not been chosen or built yet.
environment_plan.video_decoding: The published SLTUNET training path consumes precomputed SMKD sign features in .h5 files rather than decoding video, so no video decoder is introduced for it. The upstream SMKD feature-extraction step does read frames and is where simple-video-utils would apply if that step is rerun.
environment_plan.planned_first_check: Evaluation-path preflight using the authors' released PHOENIX artifacts: run the shipped infer.sh against the PHOENIX videos already in the shared Volume, using signemb_ckpt/average.pt and the checkpoint-averaged SLTUNET model, then score with eval/metrics.py against the Table 4 end-to-end test numbers. This needs no MuST-C and no SMKD pretraining, so it is unblocked by the open data gates, and it validates the TensorFlow 1.15 container, the decoding settings, and the metric implementation before any expensive run. Its result is artifact verification, not a reproduction of the authors' training.
environment_plan.container: TensorFlow 1.15 and PyTorch must coexist in one process: main.py inference() imports smkd.sign_embedder.SignEmbedding, which is PyTorch, and feeds its output into the TensorFlow graph. The base image is the public tensorflow/tensorflow:1.15.5-gpu-py3 with torch 1.7.1+cu101 and opencv-python-headless added. The NGC tf1 images would allow newer GPUs but nvcr.io returned HTTP 401 for anonymous manifest requests, and obtaining registry credentials is a secrets gate, so it was not pursued. Because the image is CUDA 10, the GPU must be Turing or older; the run uses T4. The repository's standard GPU base image is not used, since it supplies NGC PyTorch rather than TensorFlow 1.15.
environment_plan.undeclared_dependencies: The repository README declares only python==3.8 and tensorflow==1.15 and ships no requirements file or lockfile. The inference path needs five further packages that are never declared: ctcdecode (smkd/utils/decode.py; a C++ PyTorch extension published on GitHub, not PyPI, pinned here at commit c90ad94a0b19554f80804fb7812f2a1447a34a70 and built from source), pyarrow (smkd/dataset/dataloader_video.py), h5py (smkd/seq_scripts.py and data.py), scipy (smkd/utils/video_augmentation.py) and portalocker (eval/sacrebleu.py). After the second failure these were found by scanning every import in the repository rather than by discovering them one failed run at a time. pandas, sign_language_datasets and tensorflow_datasets are imported only by the preprocessing and DGS3-T scripts and are not installed; jactorch is guarded by a try/except with a vendored fallback and is not installed. Installing missing dependencies is environment work, so the attempt remains at preference level 1 with no patch to the authors' code.
build_failures_resolved: apt-get update exited 100 because the 2019-era base image pins NVIDIA CUDA apt repositories whose signing key NVIDIA rotated in 2022 ('repository is no longer signed'). Resolved by removing /etc/apt/sources.list.d/cuda.list and nvidia-ml.list; the CUDA runtime is already in the image.

pip could not resolve torch==1.7.1+cu101 because download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html is a find-links page rather than a PEP 503 index. Resolved by passing it as find_links (-f) instead of --extra-index-url.

Every container exited with 'Unknown option: --' because Modal's in-container runtime requires Python >= 3.9 while TensorFlow 1.15 requires <= 3.7 and the image ships 3.6. Resolved by running the work in a Modal Sandbox, which executes a command directly and does not host Modal's runtime inside the container.

environment_plan.artifact_staging: The in-container download of the released artifact from data.statmt.org stalled at 189.5 KiB of 967.1 MiB and did not advance over a 60-second measurement window, leaving a GPU idle. The run was stopped and the already-verified local copy was uploaded into the paper's results Volume at artifacts/phoenix.tar.gz with 'modal volume put'. run_inference.py verifies sha256 b0e708b7abe5689475905ad11ac578abb02eb0f9bf00b207bbd6d4342afe5152 before use and skips the download when the file is present, so the bytes are identical to the authors' release and later runs do not depend on that host.
environment_plan.scoring_defect_found_and_fixed: The first full pass scored B@4 22.35 against a published 28.47. The cause was in this attempt's scoring step, not in the model or the data. Upstream applies BPE removal only inside evalu.eval_metric, which strips '@@ ' from hypotheses and references; the --mode infer path used here writes output through evalu.dump_tanslation (main.py line 538), which does not strip it. Scoring that raw file counted BPE continuation markers as wrong tokens on 177 of 642 lines (429 markers), costing about 5.5 BLEU. run_inference.py now reproduces upstream's exact transformation, line.replace('@@ ', ''), before scoring. This is a fix to this attempt's glue code; the authors' code is unmodified and the attempt remains at preference level 1.

conditional_evidence.what_it_is: Decoding the PHOENIX-2014T test split with the authors' own released checkpoint-averaged SLTUNET model and released SMKD sign-embedding model, through their pinned inference entry point, scored with their own metric code. This verifies the released artifact and this attempt's evaluation pipeline.
conditional_evidence.what_it_is_not: It is not a reproduction of the authors' training. No SLTUNET or SMKD training was performed, so it cannot close any target, however close the numbers are. It also reads a lossy re-encoding of the sign videos rather than the original frames, which is a second reason it is conditional.
deviations: Sign video source is the shared Volume's HEVC re-encodings, not the original PNG frames the published numbers used (gate phoenix-frame-fidelity).
Model weights are the authors' released artifacts rather than weights trained by this attempt.
conditional_evidence.signature_check: Both signatures match the paper's Appendix A.1 exactly, so the metric implementation and version are the ones the paper reports.
conditional_evidence.independent_corroboration: Output line 2 of the test split is character-identical to the SLTUNET generation printed in the paper's own Table 10 case study: 'am donnerstag in küstennähe regen sonst mal sonne mal wolken im wechsel dann am freitag ähnliches wetter'. Reproducing a published generated sentence exactly is strong evidence that the decoding configuration, vocabulary, checkpoint and input ordering are correct.
conditional_evidence.residual_gap_hypothesis: The remaining shortfall of about 0.4 to 0.6 across every metric is unexplained. The reference construction has been ruled out by direct comparison against the authors released reference (642/642 identical lines). The leading remaining hypothesis is the lossy frame source, since the sign encoder consumes raw pixels; hardware and library nondeterminism is a second, smaller candidate. The discriminating experiment is to rerun this identical pipeline on the original PNG frames and compare, held at gate phoenix-frame-fidelity. No parameter was adjusted to narrow this gap and none should be.
conditional_evidence.reference_provenance_check: The references used for scoring were built from the PHOENIX annotation CSV rather than from a released reference file. On 2026-09-13 they were compared line by line against the authors own sltunet_ckpt/test.bpe.de from the released tarball, with BPE removed as evalu.eval_metric does: 642 of 642 lines are character-identical. The reference construction is therefore eliminated as a source of the residual gap.
conditional_evidence.eval_path_note: The authors canonical evaluation path is example/test.sh, i.e. run.py --mode test, which scores internally through evalu.eval_metric and strips BPE from hypotheses and references in one step. That path consumes precomputed SMKD features as test.h5, which the shared Volume does not hold, so this attempt used run.py --mode infer, the path the authors released infer.sh uses to decode from raw video, followed by their own eval/metrics.py. Both decode and metric code are the authors; only the join between them is this attempt, which is where the BPE defect arose.

compute_preflight.platform: Modal Sandbox, profile repro-sign, 1x T4 (15,360 MiB), 8 CPU, 32 GB
compute_preflight.what_was_measured: SMKD sign-encoder training on real PHOENIX-2014T video from the shared Volume, using the authors baseline.yaml at its stated batch_size of 2, with nvidia-smi sampling peak GPU memory. A 200-sequence training subset was used so that per-step cost is measured at steady state; subsetting changes the number of steps, not their cost.
compute_preflight.terminal: FAILED with CUDA out of memory at roughly step 83 of 100 in the first epoch: "Tried to allocate 90.00 MiB (GPU 0; 14.56 GiB total capacity; 13.43 GiB already allocated; 31.81 MiB free)". The failure is sequence-length dependent, since shorter clips completed and a longer one exhausted memory.
compute_preflight.conclusion: SMKD training does not fit on a T4 at the authors published batch size. This is not a tuning problem: the authors baseline.yaml sets device 0,1, so their run had roughly twice the memory pool available. Reducing batch size to 1 would change effective batch and therefore optimisation semantics, which AGENTS.md forbids doing silently, and would also double wall time.
compute_preflight.implication: The TensorFlow 1.15 constraint forces CUDA 10, which on Modal means T4 is the only usable accelerator, and T4 cannot run the expensive stage. However SMKD is PyTorch and SLTUNET is TensorFlow, and for TRAINING they are separate processes joined only by .h5 feature files; only the inference path loads both in one process. SMKD pretraining and feature extraction can therefore run in a modern PyTorch container on a large-memory GPU, with SLTUNET training staying in the TF 1.15 container on T4. That removes the CUDA 10 limit from the stage that actually needs the memory and the speed.
compute_preflight.still_unmeasured: SLTUNET transformer training step time and memory. The preflight targeted SMKD because it dominates the estimate and was least grounded. SLTUNET trains on precomputed features and is a 36.8M parameter model, so it is expected to be far cheaper, but that is an expectation and not a measurement.

split_container_test.hypothesis: SMKD is PyTorch and SLTUNET is TensorFlow 1.15, and for training they are separate processes joined only by .h5 feature files, so SMKD pretraining can run on a modern PyTorch stack with a large-memory GPU while SLTUNET training stays in the CUDA 10 container. That would lift the T4 memory ceiling off the expensive stage.
validated: A100-SXM4-40GB allocates and is usable through the repro-sign workspace.
torch 1.13.1+cu117 reports device capability (8, 0), i.e. Ampere is supported, unlike the CUDA 10 stack which caps at Turing.
ctcdecode at the pinned 2021 commit c90ad94a compiles successfully against torch 1.13.1, which was the main compatibility risk in this plan.
The authors released SMKD checkpoint signemb_ckpt/average.pt, saved under torch 1.7, loads without error under torch 1.13.1 (log line "Loading model finished").
six and pandas are additionally required on a slim modern base; they came free with the TensorFlow image.
split_container_test.not_validated: SMKD training throughput and peak memory on A100 were NOT measured. After the model and data loaded, the training subprocess produced no progress output and did not terminate at its 420 second timeout. The run was stopped manually rather than left to burn A100 time to the one hour function timeout.
split_container_test.leading_hypothesis_for_the_hang: A DataLoader/OpenCV fork deadlock on the modern stack. baseline.yaml sets num_worker: 10, and the same code progressed normally to step 83 under the older image (python 3.6, opencv 4.6, torch 1.7). Modern OpenCV spawns more internal threads by default and forked DataLoader workers can deadlock on its locks. The cheap next test is cv2.setNumThreads(0) and/or num_worker 0 or 2, neither of which changes optimisation semantics since dataloader parallelism does not affect the model.
split_container_test.status: promising but unproven; the memory ceiling problem on T4 remains unsolved in practice

sltunet_training_step.platform: Modal Sandbox, repro-sign, 1x T4, TF 1.15 container
sltunet_training_step.method: Throughput measurement, not a scientific run. Real SMKD features were extracted for 300 PHOENIX train sequences with the released encoder, combined to the <idx>_<aug> key form that example/sign_feature_cmb.py produces, and paired with real glosses and translations BPE-encoded using the authors released ende.bpe. MT lines reuse the released test.bpe.en/de at the papers 3:1 MT:SLT ratio. run.py --mode train was then invoked with the example/train.sh hyperparameters.
sltunet_training_step.extrapolation_to_full_config: train.sh sets token_size=1600 with update_cycle=16, so a full optimiser step consumes about 25,600 tokens rather than the ~17,700 reached here; the measurement corpus is too small to fill the accumulation cycle. Scaling by measured throughput gives roughly 11 seconds per full optimiser step on T4. train.sh sets max_training_steps=30000, and GStep increments once per optimiser update, so one configuration is on the order of 330,000 seconds, about 92 GPU-hours on T4.
sltunet_training_step.consequence: This invalidates the earlier planning figure of about 5 GPU-hours per SLTUNET configuration by roughly a factor of 18. Table 2 alone, at around 24 configurations, moves from about 120 GPU-hours to roughly 2,200 on T4, and the all-tables total from about 220 to roughly 2,400. Dollar cost stays moderate at T4 rates but serial wall time becomes months, so both parallel execution and moving SLTUNET training off T4 change from optimisations into prerequisites.
sltunet_training_step.caveats: Measured on T4 only. Batches reached ~17,700 rather than 25,600 tokens, so the extrapolation assumes throughput scales with token count. Step 0 at 70 s is warmup and is excluded. Whether nvidia-tensorflow on A100 delivers the expected 4-6x has not been tested.

gpu_utilisation.interpretation: The 43.3 percent mean covers the whole 274 second run, of which roughly two minutes was TensorFlow graph construction with the GPU idle. Utilisation reaches 100 percent during stepping, implying roughly 80 percent while actually training. SLTUNET training is therefore largely GPU-bound, unlike the SMKD stage, so a faster accelerator should convert close to proportionally into wall-clock savings. The residual gap is most likely the per-sample stochastic BPE dropout, which runs in Python on CPU for 60 percent of samples.
gpu_utilisation.memory_headroom: Peak 8,476 MiB of 15,360 on T4, about 55 percent. SLTUNET training fits comfortably where SMKD training does not, so the two stages have opposite hardware constraints: SMKD needs memory and CPU decode throughput, SLTUNET needs GPU compute.

compute_preflight.gpu_choice_conclusion: Measured, not assumed. SMKD feature extraction and training are data-loading bound: 0.25 s per sequence with dataloader workers versus 1.4 to 1.7 s single-worker, a six-fold swing from CPU-side HEVC decode and LANCZOS resize alone, so more CPU cores help there more than a faster GPU, though SMKD training also needs more than a T4 has because it OOMs at the published batch size. SLTUNET training is the opposite: it reaches 100 percent GPU utilisation while stepping and uses only 55 percent of T4 memory, so it is the stage where a faster accelerator pays off nearly proportionally. Since SLTUNET training dominates the total at about 92 GPU-hours per configuration, moving it off T4 via the anonymously available nvidia-tensorflow CUDA 11 wheels is the single highest-value speedup available.

dead_ends.topic: Running inference on the original PHOENIX PNG frames
dead_ends.status: unresolved as of 2026-09-15; the data is in place but no number was produced
dead_ends.why_it_matters: This is the discriminating experiment for the unexplained ~0.56 BLEU shortfall seen when decoding from the lossy HEVC re-encodings. The reference construction has already been ruled out (642/642 lines identical to the authors released reference), leaving the frame source as the leading untested hypothesis.
attempts: Direct reads from the shared Volume. Cold small-file reads measured 186 ms each and the test split is roughly 96,000 PNGs. The run was stopped on the assumption it had stalled; that judgement was probably wrong, because the local log buffers and the same misreading happened repeatedly in this session.

Bulk staging to container-local disk with a 32-way parallel cp. No measurable progress in about 1.5 hours, indicating the FUSE mount degrades under concurrent small reads rather than overlapping their latency.

Streaming the original RWTH archive straight into tar, which is one sequential read instead of ~96,000 random ones. Failed instantly because the TensorFlow 1.15 image is Ubuntu 18.04 whose curl 7.58 predates --retry-all-errors. The fallback then silently degraded to the slow Volume copy instead of failing loudly, which hid the real error for a long time. Switched to wget.

A latent off-by-one found by inspection rather than by running: tar --strip-components=4 leaves paths as test/<seq>/<frame>.png while the staged lookup expects <seq>/<frame>.png. Corrected to 5. This would have failed verification even after a successful download.
recommended_next_steps: Run with --limit 20 first. It exercises the identical staging, loader and scoring path in minutes rather than an hour, and would have caught three of the four failures above immediately.

If the question is specifically whether lossy frames change the score, a paired PNG-versus-MP4 run on the same subset isolates that effect directly and needs no full-test run. The full 642-sequence PNG pass is only required for a number comparable to the published 28.47.
Never let the staging fallback run silently: a failed fast path should raise rather than degrade into an hours-long slow path.
